spec.sequence: Coming east along the track, the banners show on the hill first, then the tent line, then the barricade across half the track below it.
spec.wayfinding: The track runs under the bench; a footpath climbs from the barricade to the fire.

spec.sequence: Coming down the track from the north to the stream, the barricade stands at the junction ahead and the tents above it on the right.
spec.wayfinding: The junction is at the stream; the barricade is a few steps west of it.

spec.value: A Legion column left unpaid at the recall never marched home; its grandsons keep the roster and the colours.
They keep watches, wear the colours and call what they take a levy.
Gideon will not pay to clear them. The toll company would rather use them.
A bench on the hill above a junction of two tracks, out of sight of the Gideon road, with the stream's ravine below it for a retreat.
Would disband inside a season if Gideon offered them a pardon and a wage.

sockets.why: The serjeant keeps his own tent's mouth after dark.
The serjeant stands at his tent's mouth, where the column reports and the levy is counted.
The column eats what it has at the fire.
The column sits out the night on the bench by the fire.
The man on watch steps out from the barricade and asks for the levy.
The pay book in the command tent, with the last entry in it.
The duty roster nailed to the aspen in the gap of the palisade below the tents, kept up in a clerk's hand.
The toll office's published schedules, copied out and kept with the pay book.
The roster tree in the gap of the palisade, where LF21's parley over the pardon is held.
The serjeant commands what is left of the column from the command tent.

The spring-fed tarn below the bench, where the column draws its water.
